text:
Maya (infra): heads-up: we've been seeing higher-than-usual streaming token jitter from one Dedicated pool in us-west-2 since ~02:00 UTC. p99 token latency spikes and some grpc deadlines.

Raj: saw that. symptom is tokens arriving out of order / bursts, right?

Maya (infra): yep — stream output looks fine until burst then a chunk arrives late and causes clients to hit RPC deadline. not full disconnects, just reordering and jitter.

Linus: any recent infra changes to that pool? kernel, NIC firmware, MTU knobs?

Maya (infra): pushed NIC firmware update on a subset last night (driver 5.7 -> 5.9). also we toggled SR-IOV on a handful for testing.

Raj: could be RDMA fallback path issues. when RDMA handshake fails we route over TCP and we sometimes see path MTU differences + windowing causing reordering.

Katie: quick checks i ran: tcpdump on a victim node shows a cluster of 30-40 packets delayed ~30-80ms then a bunch of retransmits. snippet: 

```
12:34:01.123456 IP nodeA > nodeB: Flags [.], seq 3544:4024, ack 782, win 64240, length 480
12:34:01.153789 IP nodeA > nodeB: Flags [.] (delayed)
12:34:01.234000 IP nodeA > nodeB: Flags [.] seq 4024:4524 (arrived out-of-order)
```

Linus: that looks like queueing inside the NIC or offload reordering. what does `ethtool -S` show?

Maya (infra): ethtool counters don't show hardware errors. ibv_devinfo shows RNIC active. ib_write_bw baseline looks ok but with high variance on these hosts.

sre-oncall-bot: alert: grpc_stream_deadline_exceeded spike on route /v1/stream/generate in us-west-2-dedicated-pool-3 — 87 events in last 10m

Raj: my hypothesis: firmware change altered packet coalescing / RSS behavior for RDMA offload; when RDMA handshake intermittently falls back to TCP we get mismatched path characteristics (MTU or QP retry) -> reordering. This especially affects token streaming which is low-rate, sensitive to out-of-order deliveries.

Katie: repro plan: 1) pin a small subset to pre-firmware image 2) run ib_write_bw + iperf3 parallel for 10m 3) enable kernel tcp_sack=0 to see SACK impact 4) capture tcpdump on both sides.

Linus: also try disabling LRO/GRO on those NICs (ethtool -K ethX gro off lro off) — that can hide reordering and cause bursty delivery that confuses grpc.

Maya (infra): rolling back firmware for 6 nodes now. patching runbook to add NIC offload tests in canary deploy.

Raj: if rollback improves p99 within 30m we can confirm. if not, check our RDMA fallback timer and grpc keepalive/deadline margins. could raise deadline as immediate mitigation.

Maya (infra): temporary mitigation: increased streaming RPC deadline from 6s -> 12s for affected pool and added automatic retry at client side. doing that in config now.

ops-bot: deploy started: infra-config/stream-deadline-bump -> us-west-2-dedicated-pool-3 (6 nodes)

Katie: after rollback + deadline bump, p99 token jitter dropped ~3x in 20m window. still seeing occasional microbursts but much better.

Linus: open action items: 1) full firmware audit for RNICs across fleet 2) add offline RDMA stress test in preflight 3) update rollout checklist to disable SR-IOV toggle without perf test 4) add ethtool/gro/LRO checks to health probe.

Maya (infra): i'll file an infra ticket with logs and assign to NICFW team. thanks all :thumbsup:

Raj: nice triage. follow-up: trace a few affected traces through our routing layer to ensure no middlebox is reordering.

Maya (infra): good call — will add packet captures from top-of-rack switches.

sre-oncall-bot: incident closed: grpc_stream_deadline_exceeded — rate returned to baseline.
